book-v1.prompt: Read together. What did Sam dig? Find the words that tell you.
book-v1.display: Sam dug a pit. A bug sat in it.

book-v1.prompt: Read together. What did Sam get wet? Point to your clue.
book-v1.display: Sam had a hat. A drip fell. His hat got wet.

beans-v1.prompt: Set five beans beside five cups. Grown-up, leave one cup empty and one with two beans. Ask your child to give each cup exactly one.
Make a circle with five cups. Grown-up, invite your child to drop one bean in each cup as you count together. Start at a different cup and count again.

drums-v1.prompt: Tap one knee, clap, then tap the other knee. Invite your child to echo the sequence.
Let your child change one movement. Copy it together twice.
Tap your shoulders twice, then clap once. Invite your child to copy you slowly.
Trade roles. Echo your child’s pattern, then ask them to lead it once more.

story-v1.prompt: Read together. What might Kit do to remember summer?
story-v1.display: The last strawberry was ripe. Kit wanted to eat it. Gran wanted to paint a picture of it.

story-v1.prompt: How did Kit help both wishes come true? Imagine another way.
story-v1.display: Kit held the berry still while Gran painted. Then they ate it together.

story-v1.prompt: Read together. What might the friends decide?
story-v1.display: Kit and Mo had one strawberry and two bowls. Mo had promised some fruit to Dad.

story-v1.prompt: Why did the friends change their plan? Tell a new ending.
story-v1.display: Kit fetched Dad. They sat on the step and shared three little slices.

shadow-v1.prompt: Point the flashlight at the wall. Hold your toy sideways and predict how its outline will change when you turn it.
Keep the light still. Turn the toy a little at a time. Describe the widest and narrowest shadows.
Hold the light behind your toy. Predict which way the shadow will move if the light shifts sideways.
Keep your toy still and move the light left, then right. Ask your child to point out what changed.

snail-v1.display: Pip found a parcel marked “For Bee, by the oak.” A moth waved from a rose.

snail-v1.prompt: Why did Pip ask for a leaf?
snail-v1.display: The parcel split. Three seeds rolled out. Pip asked Moth for a leaf to wrap them in.

snail-v1.prompt: How can you tell Bee opened the parcel?
snail-v1.display: At the oak, Bee untied the leaf. Three seeds fell into her cup.
The card showed a pond and said “For Frog.” Pip first tried a dry log.
The path ended at deep water. Duck offered Pip a ride across on her back.

snail-v1.prompt: Which detail shows Frog liked the card?
snail-v1.display: Frog read the card twice. He smiled and pinned it beside his door.
